reproduction_target: Computational reproduction of the plasmid Fiber-seq analyses: PacBio HiFi read alignment to a combined linearized-plasmid + hg38 reference (pbmm2/minimap2), m6A/nucleosome footprint calling (fibertools-rs) and CpG methylation (jasmine), full-length-fiber filtering, FIRE regulatory-element calling on genomic samples, FiberHMM sub-nucleosomal footprint calling, plasmid-vs-genomic nucleosome-density comparison, lowly/intermediately/highly chromatinized read categorization, ENCODE CTCF/DNase footprint comparison for genomic promoters, and the LDLR MPRA subsample/z-score/BH-FDR statistical analysis (author fiberseq_MPRA package).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods, now cross-checked at line level against the author repo github.com/StergachisLab/Plasmid-Fiber-seq (read via GitHub API tree + raw file fetch, no data downloaded). The repo is richer than the Stage-1 landing-page read indicated: it ships (1) two conda env EXPORTS with full package=version=build strings (environments/plasmid_fiberseq.yml, environments/FiberHMM.yml), (2) actual processing/analysis scripts (plasmid_fiberseq_processing/plasmid_fiberseq_processing.py + analysis_scripts/{pyft_analysis,add_nc_tag,call_variants_multi}.py), (3) the fiberseq_MPRA Python package with a complete runnable end-to-end LDLR script (test/ldlr_full_analysis.sh) and a bundled LDLR footprint test subset, (4) FiberHMM_functions.py, and (5) the linearized plasmid reference FASTAs (linear_plasmid_reference_sequences/*.fa) plus SnapGene plasmid maps (plasmid_maps/*.dna) — i.e. the plasmid alignment-reference inputs Stage-1 flagged as undeposited ARE in the repo. Upstream alignment (pbmm2), m6A calling (fibertools-rs), CpG calling (jasmine) and FIRE are NOT scripted in-repo; the in-repo scripts consume already-aligned, already-m6A-called BAMs via pyft/pysam (the aligner reference is recovered from the BAM @PG header, not fetched in code). Wet-lab plasmid/cell/library generation counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Read alignment of plasmid Fiber-seq HiFi reads to a combined linearized-plasmid + hg38 reference (pbmm2=1.14.99, minimap2=2.28 BUILD-STRING pinned in environments/plasmid_fiberseq.yml; no in-repo alignment wrapper, reference path recovered from BAM @PG header in plasmid_fiberseq_processing.py)

m6A methylation & nucleosome footprint identification (fibertools-rs) + CpG methylation calling (jasmine, PacBio) — NOT covered by either shipped conda export, no version in prose (only pyft==0.2.2 python bindings are pinned, not the fibertools-rs `ft` caller or jasmine)
Full-length fiber filtering (reference length +/-50 bp, >=10% m6A methylation) for downstream plasmid analysis (pyft==0.2.2 pinned in plasmid_fiberseq.yml pip section)
FIRE (Fiber-seq Inferred Regulatory Elements) calling on genomic samples via the FIRE pipeline (ref 39) — not in either shipped env export, no version in prose, not invoked in in-repo code

FiberHMM sub-nucleosomal footprint calling on plasmid samples (ref 21; FiberHMM_functions.py in repo; environments/FiberHMM.yml conda export ships hmmlearn=0.2.5, scikit-learn=1.5.2, numpy=1.26.4 etc. all with build strings)
Plasmid-vs-genomic nucleosome-density comparison (pyft nucleosome footprints via analysis_scripts/pyft_analysis.py; genomic fibers length-matched +/-50 bp, >=2 FIRE peaks)
Categorization of lowly/intermediately/highly chromatinized reads (benchmark slope 0.005 nucleosomes/bp; <20% = lowly, >60% = highly; pyft-based)

ENCODE CTCF/DNase footprint comparison for genomic promoters (CTCF ChIP-seq HEK293 ENCSR000DTW; DNase-seq HEK293T ENCSR000EJR) — accessions appear ONLY in Methods prose; grep of the entire repo finds ZERO ENCSR/ENCODE references in code (no in-code accession pin, no fetch script)

LDLR MPRA statistical analysis (author fiberseq_MPRA package v1.0.0 + FiberHMM footprint beds): 5,000-read subsamples x10,000, WT-vs-variant footprint-occupancy z-scores, one-tailed p, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 5%. Complete runnable script (test/ldlr_full_analysis.sh) + bundled LDLR footprint test subset (fp_WT_bed/ + LDLR_pure_SNVs/*.bed.gz) + GRCh38_LDLR.tsv (Kircher et al) all in repo; runtime deps (numpy=1.26.4, scipy=1.13.1, scikit-learn=1.5.2, pandas=2.2.3) build-string pinned in environments/FiberHMM.yml

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Code-check confirms Lever 1 (software_env_lock)=TRUE: both environments/*.yml are `conda env export` outputs with full package=version=build strings (linux-64 only) — a static closure for that platform. This upgrades the version axis to 2 for every step whose toolchain is IN the lock (C1 pbmm2/minimap2; C3/C6/C7 pyft; C5 FiberHMM/hmmlearn; C9 fiberseq_MPRA runtime deps). ONE step reaches R★: C9 (LDLR MPRA statistics) — author package + complete runnable script + bundled footprint test subset + bundled reference TSV, with a build-string-locked toolchain that statically covers the step. The other 8 do NOT reach R★: C1-C7 are blocked on the DATA axis (data=0) because the study publishes NO Data Availability statement and NO GEO/SRA/ENA accession for its own PacBio Fiber-seq reads or processed fibers — real env lock cannot rescue a step that has no runnable data. C2 (fibertools-rs+jasmine) and C4 (FIRE) are additionally uncovered by the lock (floating). C8 (ENCODE) has public data (data=2) but the ENCSR accessions are prose-only (grep of the repo = zero ENCODE references in code) → env_capture B, caps at RI.
